title: A high-throughput LC-MS/MS method for the measurement of the bile acid/salt content in microbiome-derived sample sets
author: Horvath, Haidacher, et al.

steps.title: Prepare D4‑CA and D4‑DCA stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make two individual internal‑standard (IS) stock solutions at ~10 mg/mL: dissolve D4‑cholic acid (D4‑CA) in Optima LC/MS‑grade water and dissolve D4‑deoxycholic acid (D4‑DCA) in a 1:2 dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO):water mixture. Aliquot and store frozen at –80 °C. If D4‑DCA appears insoluble, vortex at 2000 RPM for 5 min and gently heat at 70 °C for 1 min in a block heater before aliquoting.

steps.title: Prepare combined IS intermediate solution
steps.instruction: Dilute appropriate volumes of the D4‑CA and D4‑DCA stock solutions into 1:1 methanol:water to obtain a combined IS intermediate solution containing 500 ng/mL of each IS. Store refrigerated at +4 °C when not in use.

steps.title: Prepare Working IS‑A (WIS‑A) solution
steps.instruction: Mix equal volumes of the combined IS intermediate solution and 1:1 methanol:water to give 250 ng/mL of each IS component (D4‑CA and D4‑DCA). Store at +4 °C and discard after 1 week. This solution will be used as the diluent for all microbiome samples prior to analysis.

steps.title: Prepare Working IS‑B (WIS‑B) solution
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 1:1 methanol:water to 9 mL of the WIS‑A solution, yielding 225 ng/mL of each IS component. Store at +4 °C and discard after 1 week. Use this solution as the diluent for preparing CA, DCA, and TCA working analyte solutions and for serially‑diluted LC‑MS/MS calibration standards.

steps.title: Prepare CA, DCA, and TCA stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve cholic acid (CA), deoxycholic acid (DCA), and taurocholic acid (TCA) separately in water to ~100 mg/mL. Aliquot and store frozen at –80 °C. If any salt is insoluble, vortex at 2000 RPM for 5 min and gently heat at 70 °C for 1 min to re‑solubilize.

steps.title: Prepare combined analyte intermediate solution
steps.instruction: Dilute appropriate volumes of the CA, DCA, and TCA stock solutions into water to obtain a combined analyte intermediate solution containing 10.0 mg/mL of each compound. Sub‑aliquot into 100 µL portions and store frozen at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Working Analyte solution
steps.instruction: Dilute an appropriate volume of the combined analyte intermediate solution with the WIS‑B solution to reach 100 µg/mL of each analyte (CA, DCA, TCA). Store refrigerated at +4 °C and discard after 1 week.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards (Calibrators)
steps.instruction: Serially dilute the Working Analyte solution with WIS‑B according to Table 1 to generate calibrators A–F. Store refrigerated at +4 °C and discard after 1 week.

substeps.instruction: Calibrator F: 1000 ng/mL – 10 µL Working Analyte + 990 µL WIS‑B
Calibrator E: 250 ng/mL – 100 µL Working Analyte + 300 µL WIS‑B
Calibrator D: 62.5 ng/mL – 100 µL Working Analyte + 300 µL WIS‑B
Calibrator C: 15.6 ng/mL – 100 µL Working Analyte + 300 µL WIS‑B
Calibrator B: 3.90 ng/mL – 100 µL Working Analyte + 300 µL WIS‑B
Calibrator A: 0.977 ng/mL – 100 µL Working Analyte + 300 µL WIS‑B

steps.title: Collect and process bioreactor samples
steps.instruction: Harvest bacterial cultures from MBRA bioreactor devices. Pellet cells by centrifugation at 3000 g for 5 min. Filter the clarified supernatant through a 0.2 µm PVDF membrane filter plate by centrifugation at 200 g for 5 min. Store filtered samples frozen at –80 °C until shipment to the Texas Children’s Microbiome Center Mass Spectrometry Laboratory (TCMC‑MSL).

steps.title: Collect and process mouse stool samples
steps.instruction: Weigh 30–60 mg fecal pellets from human‑microbiota‑associated mice and resuspend in 250 µL phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS). Centrifuge at 20 000 g for 1 min and transfer the clarified supernatant to a new tube. Resuspend the remaining pellet in 250 µL absolute ethanol (200 proof) and centrifuge again at 20 000 g for 1 min. Combine equal volumes of the PBS supernatant and the ethanolic supernatant, filter through a 0.2 µm PVDF membrane filter plate by centrifugation at 200 g for 5 min, and store the filtered sample frozen at –80 °C until shipment to TCMC‑MSL.

steps.title: Prepare Mobile Phase A (MPA)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.631 g ammonium formate in 1 L Optima LC/MS‑grade water in a 1 L HPLC solvent reservoir bottle. Swirl vigorously until fully dissolved. Store the solution tightly sealed at ambient temperature; discard after 1 month.

steps.title: Prepare Mobile Phase B (MPB)
steps.instruction: Use pure Optima LC/MS‑grade acetonitrile as Mobile Phase B. Store tightly sealed at ambient temperature; this solvent does not expire.

steps.title: Prepare Needlewash (NW) solution
steps.instruction: Mix equal volumes of water and Optima LC/MS‑grade methanol in an HPLC solvent reservoir bottle. Swirl vigorously, then degas by sonication. Store tightly sealed at ambient temperature; this solution does not expire.

steps.title: Set up LC column and guard column
steps.instruction: Install a Raptor C18 analytical column (2.7 µm SPP particles, 100 mm × 2.1 mm ID, 90 Å pore) and an Ultra C18 guard column (5.0 µm silica, 10 mm × 2.1 mm ID, 100 Å pore) on the LC system.

steps.title: Configure needle rinse program
steps.instruction: Program the Nexera X2 MP autosampler to perform external rinsing only, both before and after sample aspiration, using 500 µL of Needlewash solution each time.

steps.title: Set chromatographic gradient and temperatures
steps.instruction: Set column temperature to 50 °C and autosampler tray temperature to 15 °C. Use a flow rate of 0.30 mL/min. Apply the following gradient: 0–4.5 min, 5 %→90 % MPB; 4.5–5.5 min, hold at 90 % MPB; 5.5–5.6 min, linear decrease 90 %→5 % MPB; 5.6–8.0 min, hold at 5 % MPB. Total cycle time is 8.4 min with an initial back‑pressure of ~2200 psi. Program the 6500 QTRAP divert valve: 0–1.0 min divert to waste (position B); 1.0–8.0 min divert to MS source (position A); 8.0–8.4 min divert to waste (position B). Typical retention times: TCA ≈3.1 min, CA ≈3.6 min, DCA ≈4.25 min.

steps.title: Configure ESI source parameters
steps.instruction: Install the TurboIonSpray® electrospray ionization probe in the Turbo V™ ion source and set: polarity = negative; curtain gas = 20; TurboIonSpray voltage = ‑4500 V; source temperature = 250 °C; Gas 1 (nebulizer) = 40; Gas 2 (heater) = 50.

steps.title: Set MS operational parameters
steps.instruction: Set collisionally activated dissociation (CAD) gas pressure to ‘High’; declustering potential = ‑40 V; entrance potential = ‑8 V; collision‑cell exit potential = ‑10 V; Q1 resolution = unit; Q3 resolution = unit. Apply the molecule‑specific transitions listed in Table 3.

substeps.instruction: Cholic acid: Q1 = 407 → Q3 = 343, dwell = 4 ms, CE = ‑47 V
Cholic acid: Q1 = 407 → Q3 = 289, dwell = 4 ms, CE = ‑52 V
Cholic acid‑D4: Q1 = 411 → Q3 = 347, dwell = 4 ms, CE =‑47 V
Cholic acid‑D4: Q1 = 411 → Q3 = 290, dwell = 4 ms, CE =‑52 V
Deoxycholic acid: Q1 = 391 → Q3 = 345, dwell = 4 ms, CE =‑47 V
Deoxycholic acid: Q1 = 391 → Q3 = 355, dwell = 4 ms, CE =‑46 V
Deoxycholic acid‑D4: Q1 = 395 → Q3 = 349, dwell = 4 ms, CE =‑47 V
Deoxycholic acid‑D4: Q1 = 395 → Q3 = 359, dwell = 4 ms, CE =‑46 V
Taurocholic acid: Q1 = 514 → Q3 = 124, dwell = 14 ms, CE =‑64 V
Taurocholic acid: Q1 = 514 → Q3 = 107, dwell = 14 ms, CE =‑64 V

steps.title: Calculate calibration curves and performance metrics
steps.instruction: For each analyte, plot the instrument response ratio (IR = A_analyte / A_IS) versus nominal calibrator concentration and perform a weighted (1/x) least‑squares linear regression. Record the equations and statistics: CA : IR = 0.00526 × [CA] + 0.00651 (R² = 0.991); TCA : IR = 2310 × [TCA] + 3045 (R² = 0.9856); DCA : IR = 0.00337 × [DCA] + 0.00641 (R² = 0.999). Determine LOD and LOQ using the standard deviation of the y‑intercepts and the mean slope: D4‑CA LOD = 0.20 ng/mL, LOQ = 0.63 ng/mL; TCA LOD = ‑0.76 ng/mL, LOQ = 2.32 ng/mL; D4‑DCA LOD = 1.1 ng/mL, LOQ = 3.4 ng/mL. Note that a commercial D4‑TCA internal standard was not available.
